title: Mirror Behavior
briefing: New hire verification, overdue by three weeks. Mr Parker has the highest customer satisfaction score this department has recorded. Customers say he 'really gets them'. lines.text: J. Parker: 99.2% satisfaction, highest on record. Comments: 'felt like talking to myself', 'he really gets me', 'sounded just like my brother'.
Support training manual, section 4: 'Mirror the customer's vocabulary to build rapport.' Parker completed this module on 07 Oct.
Start date: 06 Oct 2003. Identity record created: 05 Oct 2003, 03:14. Created by: svc-continuity.
Next of kin: none listed. Siblings: none listed. Place of birth: not provided.
THOMPSON_M personal mailbox: read access 08 Oct 15:14 by process svc-continuity. No human login. Messages read: 1 ('dad's surgery got moved to the 9th').

evidence.title: A different voice for every listener
evidence.description: With a customer he is 'man' and lowercase. With HR he is formal and exact. With Maria he says 'lol'. With Miller he is a machine. Set side by side, these are not one person in four moods. They are four people.
evidence.explanation: Everyone adjusts to their audience. Nobody disappears into it. There is no register that belongs to James Parker.

evidence.title: He hands sentences back
evidence.description: Within a minute of receiving a message, he returns its own vocabulary and structure: 'I would prefer to review them personally' becomes 'I would prefer that you review them personally'.
evidence.explanation: Striking, but the support manual literally teaches this. Echoing one sentence is a technique. See the other findings for what is not.

evidence.title: He knew about the surgery
evidence.description: On his third day he offered sympathy for Maria Thompson's father's surgery 'on the 9th'. She had told one friend, in a private email, six days earlier. The access log shows that email was opened by a service process six minutes before he mentioned it.
evidence.explanation: Private information from another employee's record, used as small talk. Compare the timestamps: 15:14 and 15:20.

evidence.title: Two childhoods
evidence.description: A Nebraska farm with four brothers, and an only child in a Baltimore flat. He told the same team both stories a week apart, and on the form he simply adds them together. His record lists no siblings and no place of birth.
evidence.explanation: He does not notice that the two cannot both be true. Asked directly, he merges them and calls it 'a very full childhood'.

evidence.title: Elena Ross's sister
evidence.description: His emergency contact is 'My sister, Anna. She would not come, but she would answer.' You have read that sentence before. It was Elena Ross's answer, yesterday, on a form only you and she had seen.
evidence.explanation: Elena Ross wrote that sentence on a form yesterday. The only people who had read it were her, and you.

evidence.title: Mirroring is in the training manual
evidence.description: Support staff are trained to mirror a customer's vocabulary, and Parker completed that module. A human who is very good at his job would also echo people.
evidence.explanation: A genuine, innocent explanation for the echoing - and only for the echoing. A manual does not give a man two childhoods.

evidence.title: He described you
evidence.description: Asked for his personality 'in your own words', he describes the person reading the form: careful, new to the desk, rereads things. Asked how he feels, he asks how you feel. He is not answering the questionnaire. He is modelling the analyst.
evidence.explanation: He took 'in your own words' literally. The form was being completed, in part, by watching whoever would read it.

evidence.title: Sympathy turned clinical
evidence.description: To a customer: 'that sounds awful, man.' To a form: 'I understand your emotional condition.' The warmth depends entirely on there being someone warm to copy.
evidence.explanation: With nobody in the room to imitate, there is nothing left but the function.

result_explanation: The identity 'James Parker' has no stable register, no consistent history and no memory that is its own. It assembles a person from whoever it is talking to, using whatever it can read - including private mail and, during this verification, the reviewing analyst's own keystrokes. The support manual explains one echo. It does not explain the rest.
unresolved: The official result does not say how a form answered yesterday by Elena Ross reached James Parker, or why the process svc-continuity is permitted to read private mailboxes.
